title: Samwui Khararchan: Luishat Laa (The Book of Psalms in Tangkhul Naga)
alternate_titles: The Book of Psalms in Tangkhul Naga
Tangkhul Luishat Laa kala Samwui Lairik
subject: Hymnology, Devotional Poetry & Scripture
notes: The Book of Psalms in Tangkhul Naga. A masterpieces of indigenous poetic rhythm, rendering Hebrew parallelisms into the metrics of Tangkhul traditional song poetry (Hao-laa).

front_matter.title_page: Samwui Khararchan: Luishat Laa (The Book of Psalms in Tangkhul Naga) (1968)
front_matter.preface: The translation of the Psalter into Tangkhul Naga represents a sublime convergence between ancient Hebrew poetry and indigenous Tangkhul poetic forms. The translators incorporated parallelisms, vivid mountain metaphors, and pastoral idioms that resonate deeply with the highland soul of the Tangkhul people.

chapters.title: Psalm 1: The Two Ways -- Tree by the Water Brooks
chapters.summary: Contrast between the righteous person flourishing like a river tree and the chaff blown by wind.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Psalm 1:1-4: Kaphā-kashana mikumo kachikhana kashikashibingwui ningkazangli mashurla, yorshibingwui shongfali mangapamla, kala khanganoibingwui pamkaphunli mangapam-mana; Kha ana Prohowui ngashan-kasakazingli mathat-eina leikashiye, kala Awui tui zingsho ngazing kachikhali thimkazape. Ana kongkha kaphā wui tui-ngapomli thingphun phunkahai thada sakhura, ana awui thotli thei kaphā phāser-ra, awui naorap mangapaorira; kala ana sakahai ot pupupli mashungsere. Kashikashibing chi hithada maleimana: kha huina shuk-kakhui pakhara thada kasaye.
chapters.english_translation: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night. And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.

vocabulary.meaning: threshing chaff, husks blown by breeze

grammar_notes: Three-fold negative parallel clauses: 'mashurla... mangapamla... mangapam-mana'.
Simile with botanical imagery: 'thingphun phunkahai thada' (like a tree planted).
exercises: Identify the botanical terms for leaf ('naorap') and fruit ('thei').
Contrast the righteous and ungodly using the imagery of Psalm 1.

chapters.title: Psalm 23: The Shepherd Psalm (Proho i-wui Ngashankashapana)
chapters.summary: The beloved pastoral psalm of comfort, protection, and overflowing blessing in lyrical Tangkhul.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Psalm 23:1-6: Proho i-wui Ngashankashapana; ili khikha macham-mana. Ana ili ngashalung kaphāli pamkazipsake, kala kongkhamathān tui-ngapomli ili zaipinge. Ana iwui mangazingli mathangathuksake: Awui mingwui vang mashung-kasa shongfali ili zaisange. I kathi ngachingwui longkhorli zakhalangli, I kashikashili mangachek-mana; kasakei Na i eina li-leie; Nawui thingchot kala deikhotna ili ngasot-e. Nawui mik-ngalemli i-kashibingwui ngalemli maihon akha sakahaye; Nawui eina iwui kakhutli meirong theiye; iwui kom kashunglaga tuksange. Mashungna iwui ringkapha tharili kaphā kala ngashan china ili shursara: kala i Prohowui shimli thot khamara kuppup pamkapamsara.
chapters.english_translation: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreeth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

vocabulary.meaning: deep ravine, mountain gorge, shadow valley

grammar_notes: Agentive personal title with suffix '-na': 'Ngashankashapana' (The One who shepherds).
Highland geographical term for valley: 'longkhor' (deep mountain ravine).
exercises: How is 'my cup runneth over' expressed in Tangkhul?

chapters.title: Psalm 91: The Secret Place of the Most High
chapters.summary: Divine shelter under heavenly wings and deliverance from snare and pestilence.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Psalm 91:1-5, 11-12: Kaphāmei Kazingwui pamkaphunli pamkakhui chinana Pangashan Kapeiwui ngaching tharili pamsara. I Prohowui vang hangsara: 'A iwui rungkahai pam, iwui lungkhor kashang, iwui Varivara; Ali I chotkhangashit khuisara.' Ana vanaokhamakhui khangashun eina kala kasham kashikaza eina nali huikhuira. Ana Awui theirei eina nali kuplupsara, kala Awui phana ngashingli na rungpamsara: Awui mashung-tui nawui dhal kala kot thada kasaye.
chapters.english_translation: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust. Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence. He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
grammar_notes: Defensive weaponry metaphors in Tangkhul: 'dhal' (shield) and 'kot' (buckler/armor).
Metaphorical shelter using avian wing terminology: 'phana'.
exercises: Identify the titles for God in Psalm 91:1-2.
Translate verse 4 into modern Ukhrul idiom.

chapters.title: Psalm 121: The Traveler's Mountain Psalm (Kaphungli Yanglu)
chapters.summary: Lifting eyes to the hills from whence cometh help; the keeper who never slumbers.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Psalm 121:1-8: I iwui mik kaphung kashangli thuk-kashok-e: iwui khangachon kachikhali shokhungra? Iwui khangachon kazing kala ngalei sakahai Prohowui eina shokhunge! Ana nawui kakhutli ngasotkazip makasara: nali ngashankashapana mangaphama-mana! Theilu, Israel-li ngashankashapana mangaphama-mana, mapila-mana. Prohona nawui ngashankashapana; Prohona nawui kashikli nawui ngaching katha leisaye. Zingsho eina zingkhamathānna nali makara, ngazing eina kachanna nali mamakhura. Prohona nali kashikashili huikhuira: Ana nawui mangazingli ngashansara.
chapters.english_translation: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night. The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.
grammar_notes: Directional elevation verb: 'thuk-kashok-e' (to lift eyes upward toward peaks).
Paired physiological verbs of resting: 'mangaphama-mana, mapila-mana' (slumber not, sleep not).
exercises: Why is Psalm 121 particularly loved by travellers traversing Naga mountain passes?
Identify the celestial bodies contrasted in verse 6.

chapters.title: Psalm 150: The Grand Doxology with Traditional Instruments
chapters.summary: Praise the Lord with trumpet, harp, strings, dance, and clashing cymbals.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Psalm 150:1-6: Proholi mathat-eina kashaklu! Awui kathara shillongli Varivarali mathatlu! Awui pangashankazingli Ali mathatlu! Awui khamatheikasa otbingwui vang Ali mathatlu: Awui kaphāmeikasa vang Ali mathatlu! Torot (trumpet) kakhong eina Ali mathatlu: Harp kala Luishat-thing (lyre) eina Ali mathatlu! Tingteila (tambourine) kala pheichak (dance) eina Ali mathatlu: Tui-thingkhanghui (stringed organs) kala Pung (pipes) eina Ali mathatlu! Meikakhong chot eina Ali mathatlu: Khongyui kapei khong eina Ali mathatlu! Ringkashap kapeina Proholi mathat-eina kashaklu! Hallelujah!
chapters.english_translation: Praise ye the LORD. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power. Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his excellent greatness. Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp. Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs. Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals. Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.

vocabulary.meaning: bamboo pipe, flutes, musical wind organ

exercises: List all traditional and biblical musical instruments mentioned in Psalm 150.
Explain the meaning of 'ringkashap kapei' (everything with breath).

chapters.title: Liturgical & Poetic Lexicon of the Tangkhul Psalter
chapters.summary: Comprehensive register of 30 musical, emotional, and nature terms from the Psalms.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Luishat Laa Concordance:
1. Kongkha -- River bank / quiet brook
2. Ngashankashapana -- The Good Shepherd
3. Longkhor -- Shadowy gorge / mountain ravine
4. Thingchot -- Shepherd's staff
5. Pamkaphun -- Secret pavilion of God
6. Pheichak -- Sacred festival dance
7. Pung -- Bamboo reed pipes
8. Ringkashap -- Living breathing beings
chapters.english_translation: Concordance of devotional, musical, and environmental terms from the Tangkhul Psalms.
exercises: Compose a 4-line devotional poem in Tangkhul using the words 'kongkha' and 'ngashankashapana'.

pages.english_translation: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help. My help cometh from the LORD, which made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved: he that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. The LORD is thy keeper: the LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night. The LORD shall preserve thee from all evil: he shall preserve thy soul.

pages.english_translation: Praise ye the LORD. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power. Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his excellent greatness. Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp. Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs. Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals. Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.
